messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert PD-3201 fired -> rule: inference-proxy-latency-us-west > 1200ms (5m). Affected: runtime-proxy-prod. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-3201

maria-sre: acked. jumping on it now — checking upstream queues and canaries :eyes:

dan-oncall: seeing a short burst on the proxy tail latency graphs, looks correlated with a synthetic canary run at ~11:03. no 5xx, just high p95/p99 token latency

alex-platform: fwiw the rolling deploy completed ~10:58, but health checks were green. can run `kubectl get pods -l app=runtime-proxy -o wide` if you want pod-level CPU/mem

maria-sre: ran quick query on seating: `sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime-proxy",le=+Inf}[5m])) by (instance)` — pattern shows a ~30s spike across 3 nodes then drops

incidentbot: PD note: incident auto-resolved by monitoring after 2m (no open triggers).

dan-oncall: confirmed auto-resolve. no customer-facing errors in logs, all user-facing traces show normal tail latency. marking as NO_IMPACT for CS / SRE notes :white_check_mark:

sre-lead: thanks — sounds transient. can we mute the synthetic canary alert while we investigate the canary's timing? we should avoid noisy pages for scheduled tests

maria-sre: agreed. creating a short-term suppress rule for the canary alert and adding a runbook link to the alert: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency

alex-platform: filing a follow-up ticket to (1) shift canary schedule by 2m to avoid overlap, (2) add a tag to PD alert so oncall sees "canary-origin" and (3) lower sensitivity for region-wide tail blips. ticket: https://tickets.internal/RW-1429

dan-oncall: leaving a reminder to monitor for 1 hour, will re-open if it re-fires. thanks team :thumbsup:

maria-sre: quick postmortem note: transient, auto-resolved, no customer impact, action items on RW-1429. closing thread.
